title: Can I look after my baby?
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on the acute medical unit. Ms Ross, 30, has had a stroke and has weakness in her left arm. Her baby is four months old.

She asks you, tearfully, whether she will be able to look after her baby.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Arrange for the occupational therapist to discuss practical support for caring for her baby.
options.detailed: Occupational therapists can help with practical adaptations. It ranks third because she needs a response from you first.

options.text: Tell her she probably won't be able to care for her baby on her own.
options.detailed: She may need help, but saying this now, without understanding her situation, could be devastating.

options.text: Ask her what worries her most, and what support she has at home.
options.brief: Understanding her worries helps you respond.
options.detailed: She may be worried about feeding, carrying the baby, or being alone. Knowing what matters most helps you respond honestly and practically.

options.text: Reassure her that she'll definitely be able to care for her baby.
options.detailed: This may be what she wants to hear, but you can't know.

options.text: Be honest that recovery is uncertain this early, and that the team will help her plan.
options.detailed: Recovery after stroke varies, especially in the early days. Being honest, and explaining that therapists will help her plan, gives her realistic hope.

explanation.issue: This tests how you respond to a patient's fears after a serious diagnosis, honestly and practically.
explanation.keyDetails: She is young and has a baby. Her recovery is uncertain. She is distressed.
explanation.reasoning: [C] explores her worries, [E] is honest, and [A] arranges practical help. [D] gives false hope, and [B] is premature.
explanation.competing: The order of [D] and [B] is close. The key ranks [B] last because it is premature and could cause unnecessary distress about something central to her life.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 2, communicating honestly and supporting patients.
